boundary_rationale: A narrated scene, not reported divine speech, opens this unit: ק֚וֹל עַל שְׁפָיִ֣ים נִשְׁמָ֔ע בְּכִ֥י תַחֲנוּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י הֶעֱוּוּ֙ אֶת דַּרְכָּ֔ם שָׁכְח֖וּ אֶת יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.3.21, byte tier) — “A voice is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and the petitions of the children of Israel; because they have perverted their way, they have forgotten Yahweh their God” (web:Jer.3.21) — shifting from the first-person divine promise of Jer.3.19 to third-person description of a sound. Yahweh’s call, שׁ֚וּבוּ בָּנִ֣ים שׁוֹבָבִ֔ים אֶרְפָּ֖ה מְשׁוּבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.3.22, byte tier) — “Return, you backsliding children, and I will heal your backsliding” (web:Jer.3.22) — is answered inside the same unit by the community’s own first-person-plural confession, “Behold, we have come to you” (web:Jer.3.22) through “we have sinned against Yahweh our God” (web:Jer.3.25), closing “We have not obeyed Yahweh our God’s voice” (web:Jer.3.25). This same three-word call, שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙, stands at Jer.3.14 (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) — identical to the call quoted above at skeleton tier and distinct at byte tier (sweep: 2 verses); the shared call argues continuity across this unit's front seam, which is carried instead by the speaker turn at Jer.3.21. A conditional address to ‘Israel’ by name, resuming Yahweh’s own voice, opens the next unit at Jer.4.1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading web:Jer.3.22's imperative opening as the true onset, with web:Jer.3.21 held back as the close of the preceding restoration promise, was considered and rejected: the voice-heard-weeping scene lacks an addressee or formula tying it to the prior unit's promise, and it motivates the call and confession that follow it rather than concluding what precedes it.

The wind-of-judgment image runs through Jer.4.12 to the invader’s approach and the communal outcry “Woe to us! For we are ruined” (web:Jer.4.13), before the vocative address to Jerusalem at Jer.4.14.

boundary_rationale: A koh-amar formula opens a fresh, explicitly marked frame after the vision report closing at Jer.4.26: כִּי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.4.27, byte tier), introducing Yahweh’s own words, “The whole land will be a desolation” (web:Jer.4.27), closing with the qualifier “I will not make a full end” (web:Jer.4.27) and the divine self-attestation at Jer.4.28, “I have spoken it” (web:Jer.4.28). Neither Jer.4.29 (the cities’ panic-flight) nor Jer.4.30 carries an imperative, named vocative, or fresh koh-amar restart distinguishing it as an independent onset from this koh-amar-opened unit; Jer.4.30 shifts to direct address of the personified city, and its ketiv/qere note’s consonantal divergence - one final yod - is carried by the unpointed ketiv, while the pointed qere the citation quotes, וְאַ֨תְּ שָׁד֜וּד מַֽה תַּעֲשִׂ֗י (oshb:Jer.4.30, byte tier), is the ordinary form actually read, “You, when you are made desolate, what will you do?” (web:Jer.4.30) - before the unit closes on the daughter of Zion’s death-cry, “Woe is me now!” (web:Jer.4.31).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reject splitting the panic-flight and personified-woman verses into their own unit: neither Jer.4.29 nor Jer.4.30 carries an imperative, vocative-noun, or koh-amar restart distinguishing it from the koh-amar-opened unit that begins at Jer.4.27. boundary_rationale: An explicit first-person speech-attribution formula opens this unit: וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי אַךְ דַּלִּ֖ים הֵ֑ם (oshb:Jer.5.4, byte tier), “Then I said,” (web:Jer.5.4) continuing “Surely these are poor” (web:Jer.5.4) - the prophet's own reasoning about the poor and “the great men” (web:Jer.5.5), who “have broken the yoke” (web:Jer.5.5) despite knowing Yahweh's way. No fresh imperative, vocative, or formula separates the shift into Yahweh's own rhetorical question at Jer.5.7 (a verse carrying a ketiv/qere note on its verb, quoted here at the qere: אֵ֤י לָזֹאת֙ ... אֶֽסְלַֽח לָ֔ךְ (oshb:Jer.5.7, byte tier), “How can I pardon you?” web:Jer.5.7) or the adultery charge that follows; the unit closes on the plea הַֽעַל אֵ֥לֶּה לוֹא אֶפְקֹ֖ד נְאֻם יְהֹוָ֑ה וְאִם֙ בְּג֣וֹי אֲשֶׁר כָּזֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִתְנַקֵּ֖ם נַפְשִֽׁי (oshb:Jer.5.9, byte tier), “Shouldn’t my soul be avenged” (web:Jer.5.9), corroborated by the neum-YHWH tag at that verse. The same plea recurs at Jer.5.29 and, under its dual qualifier, at MT 9:8 (= WEB 9:9) (sweep: 3 verses, MT keys); the Jer.5.9 and Jer.5.29 forms diverge even at skeleton tier - a plene against a defective spelling of the negative, לוֹא (oshb:Jer.5.9, byte tier) against לֹֽא (oshb:Jer.5.29, byte tier), and a vav-prefixed against a bare conditional, וְאִם֙ against אִ֚ם (oshb:Jer.5.29, byte tier) - so just the closing soul-noun tail, נַפְשִֽׁי (oshb:Jer.5.9, byte tier), is byte-shared between them.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reject splitting at the shift from third-person "them" to the divine first-person question in Jer.5.7: no imperative, vocative, or formula marks that shift as an independent onset, merely a pronominal change within the prophet's continuing reflection.

boundary_rationale: A discourse-frame imperative reopens the declare/publish pairing used to open this material at Jer.4.5: הַגִּ֥ידוּ זֹ֖את בְּבֵ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְהַשְׁמִיע֥וּהָ בִיהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.5.20, byte tier), “Declare this in the house of Jacob, and publish it in Judah” (web:Jer.5.20); the pairing itself recurs at 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses, MT keys), but the two forms are distinct spellings - the plain הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier; the verse carries a single-witness ketiv/qere note on a different word) against the vav-prefixed, suffixed וְהַשְׁמִיע֥וּהָ (oshb:Jer.5.20, byte tier) here, which stands alone at 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse, MT keys). The citation's closing word, לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.5.20, byte tier; "saying"), subordinates the imperative-plus-vocative that opens Jer.5.21 as the content of this commissioned speech, so it does not open a fresh unit. The commissioned proclamation runs through the charge of blind, deaf unresponsiveness, “who have eyes, and don’t see” (web:Jer.5.21), and two parallel illustrations of Yahweh's constancy against the people's fickleness - the sea bound by “a perpetual decree” (web:Jer.5.22) and the rain-giver “in its season” (web:Jer.5.24) - without a further imperative, vocative, or koh-amar restart separating Jer.5.22 from Jer.5.23-Jer.5.24.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reject splitting the sea-bound and rain-giver illustrations (Jer.5.22 / Jer.5.23-Jer.5.24) at the shift from second to third person: שִׁמְעוּ נָ֣א זֹ֔את עַ֥ם סָכָ֖ל (oshb:Jer.5.21, byte tier) and הַאוֹתִ֨י לֹא תִירָ֜אוּ (oshb:Jer.5.22, byte tier) address the hearers in the second person, while וְלָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ הָיָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.5.23, byte tier) turns to third-person description, yet no imperative, vocative, or koh-amar restart marks that junction as an independent onset, so the commissioned proclamation opened at Jer.5.20 carries across the shift; WEB's own quotation-mark convention there is a disclosed tier-4 non-signal, not the ground for holding the illustrations together. Reject splitting the imperative-plus-vocative that opens Jer.5.21 into its own unit as well: לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.5.20, byte tier) closing Jer.5.20 subordinates it as the content of the very speech this unit's opening pair commissions.

boundary_rationale: A vocative-plus-imperative summons opens chapter 6: הָעִ֣זוּ בְּנֵ֣י בִניָמִ֗ן מִקֶּ֨רֶב֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.6.1, byte tier), “Flee for safety, you children of Benjamin, out of the middle of Jerusalem!” (web:Jer.6.1), continuing “evil looks out from the north” (web:Jer.6.1). Its blow-the-trumpet collocation, תִּקְע֣וּ שׁוֹפָ֔ר (oshb:Jer.6.1, byte tier), echoes the qere תִּקְע֥וּ שׁוֹפָ֖ר (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier; a single-witness ketiv/qere note stands at that verse, the spliced run being the qere against the ketiv ותקעו) at Jer.4.5 (sweep: 3 verses at accent-stripped tier, MT keys; not exclusive), and its closing colon, מִצָּפ֖וֹן וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל (oshb:Jer.6.1, byte tier), is byte-identical to מִצָּפ֖וֹן וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל (oshb:Jer.4.6, byte tier) at Jer.4.6, a string standing at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, MT keys); the opening imperative itself is a mater-lectionis pair with that same verse, plene הָעִ֖יזוּ (oshb:Jer.4.6, byte tier) at Jer.4.6 against defective הָעִ֣זוּ (oshb:Jer.6.1, byte tier) here, each spelling standing at 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse each, MT keys). The summons runs through the siege description at Jer.6.2-Jer.6.3 (shepherds pitching tents against the daughter of Zion) without a further imperative or vocative address, before the besiegers' own quoted battle-cry at Jer.6.4.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reject splitting the siege description (Jer.6.2-Jer.6.3) from the opening summons: Jer.6.2 turns to first person, דָּמִ֖יתִי (oshb:Jer.6.2, byte tier), while Jer.6.3 is third person, and neither carries an imperative, a vocative or a speech formula, so no tier-1 onset separates them from the summons.
